entities.label: The Shahnameh
entities.summary: The literary work in which the story of Zal and Rudabeh is told.

entities.label: Ferdowsi
entities.summary: The poet of the Shahnameh.

entities.label: Zal and Rudabeh
entities.summary: The story of Zal, the white-haired son of Sam, from his birth onward, in the reign of Manuchehr.

entities.label: Sam
entities.summary: A great hero of Iran, son of Nariman, who long has no child.

facts.text: Hero of Iran, father of Zal

entities.label: The mother of Zal
entities.summary: A beloved of Sam in his household, who bears him a son.

entities.label: Zal
entities.summary: The son of Sam, born with white hair; also called Dastan.

entities.label: The nurse
entities.summary: A bold nurse of Sam's household who brings him the news of his son.

entities.label: Simorgh
entities.summary: A great bird that nests on Mount Alborz.

facts.text: Bird of Alborz who raises Zal

entities.label: The feather of the Simorgh
entities.summary: A feather the Simorgh gives Zal, to be burned in fire if he is ever in need.

entities.label: Mount Alborz
entities.summary: The mountain where the Simorgh has her nest.

entities.label: Manuchehr
entities.summary: The king of Iran.

entities.label: Nowzar
entities.summary: A prince of the court of Manuchehr whom the king sends to Sam.

entities.label: Qaren
entities.summary: A great man of Manuchehr's court who sits at the king's side.

entities.label: Zabulistan
entities.summary: The land of Sam, which he entrusts to Zal.

entities.label: Gorgsaran
entities.summary: A land of enemies against which Sam leads his army.

entities.label: Mazandaran
entities.summary: A land of enemies against which Sam leads his army.

entities.label: Mehrab
entities.summary: The king of Kabul, of the line of Zahhak, who pays tribute to Sam.

entities.label: Rudabeh
entities.summary: The daughter of Mehrab, renowned for her beauty.

entities.label: Sindokht
entities.summary: The wise wife of Mehrab.

entities.label: Zahhak
entities.summary: A king of old from whom Mehrab descends.

entities.label: The maids of Rudabeh
entities.summary: Five Turkish maids who serve Rudabeh and keep her secret.

entities.label: Kabul
entities.summary: The kingdom of Mehrab.

entities.label: The go-between
entities.summary: A woman who carries messages between Zal and Rudabeh.

entities.label: Kakuy
entities.summary: A warrior who leads the enemy army against Sam.

entities.label: The Kashaf river
entities.summary: A river from which a dragon once came out, as Sam recalls.

entities.label: Sistan
entities.summary: The land of Sam's house, also called Nimruz.

entities.label: Rostam
entities.summary: The son of Zal and Rudabeh, a child of wondrous size and strength.

events.label: A son with white hair
events.summary: Sam has long had no child. A beloved of his household bears him a son as bright as the sun but with hair all white; for a week no one dares tell him, until a bold nurse brings him the news.

events.label: The child abandoned
events.summary: Seeing the white hair, Sam despairs and asks God what sin he has committed; fearing what the nobles will say of a demon's child, he has the infant carried away and left on a mountain where the Simorgh has her home.

events.label: In the nest of the Simorgh
events.summary: The Simorgh, seeking food for her young, finds the crying child on the hot rock and carries him to her nest on Alborz. God moves her to mercy; she and her young feed him, and he grows there into a tall young man whose fame spreads through the world.

events.label: Sam's dreams
events.summary: Sam dreams that a rider from India brings news of his son, and the mobads tell him that every creature raises its young and that he must seek God's pardon. In a second dream a youth with a banner appears and a man rebukes him for leaving his son to be nursed by a bird.

events.label: The Simorgh returns the son
events.summary: Sam comes to the mountain and prays for forgiveness. The Simorgh tells the young man, whom she calls Dastan, that his father has come; she gives him one of her feathers, to burn in fire if he is ever in trouble, and carries him down to Sam, who promises never again to harden his heart against him.

events.label: At the court of Manuchehr
events.summary: Manuchehr sends Nowzar to welcome Sam and receives him with Qaren beside him. Struck by Zal, he has the star-readers consult the stars, and they foretell that Zal will be a renowned hero; the king grants Sam rich gifts and a charter over Kabul, Zabul and the lands to India.

events.label: Zal left in Zabulistan
events.summary: Back in Sistan, Sam goes to war against the Gorgsaran and Mazandaran and leaves Zal in charge of Zabulistan. Zal protests at being parted from his father again, but Sam tells him the stars have set his seat there; Zal gathers the wise and learns until none in the world equals him.

events.label: A feast at Kabul
events.summary: Zal travels through his lands to Kabul, whose king, Mehrab, is of the line of Zahhak and pays tribute to Sam. Mehrab comes with gifts and they feast together; afterwards a noble tells Zal that Mehrab has a daughter brighter than the sun, and Zal is lost in thought.

entityAssociations.role: lord to whom tribute is paid

events.label: An invitation refused
events.summary: Mehrab asks Zal to honour his house with a visit. Zal declines, saying Sam and the king would not approve his drinking in the house of idol-worshippers, yet he praises Mehrab after he leaves, and his longing for the unseen daughter grows.

events.label: Rudabeh hears of Zal
events.summary: At home Sindokht asks Mehrab about the son of Sam. Mehrab praises Zal's strength, generosity and bearing, saying only his white hair is spoken against. Hearing this, Rudabeh falls in love with Zal without having seen him.

events.label: Rudabeh's confidantes
events.summary: Rudabeh tells her five maids of her love. They protest that the son of Sam was cast out by his father and raised by a bird; she rebukes them angrily, saying she wants neither Caesar nor the emperor of Chin but Zal alone, and they promise to find a way.

events.label: Roses by the river
events.summary: The maids go gathering roses by the river where Zal is camped. Zal shoots a waterbird and sends his page across for it; the maids praise their mistress to the page, and Zal, delighted, sends them gold and jewels, questions them himself and agrees to their plan to bring him to Rudabeh's palace.

events.label: The maids report
events.summary: The gatekeeper scolds the maids for going out, but they slip past. They tell Rudabeh of Zal's beauty and his promise, she teases them for changing their minds, and they prepare a chamber decked with brocade, gold and flowers.

events.label: The tresses and the lasso
events.summary: At nightfall Zal comes to the palace and Rudabeh greets him from the roof, letting down her long black tresses for him to climb. He refuses to hurt her, throws his lasso to the battlements and climbs up. They spend the night together and each swears to take no other, though Zal fears Manuchehr and Sam will not consent.

events.label: Zal writes to his father
events.summary: Zal tells his counsellors of his love; they hesitate, since Mehrab is of Zahhak's line, but advise a letter to Sam. Zal writes recalling his abandonment and Sam's promise to grant his wishes, and asks leave to marry the daughter of Mehrab.

events.label: Sam reads the letter
events.summary: A rider reaches Sam while he is hunting near the Gorgsaran. Sam is troubled: refusing would break his promise, but what lineage could come of a bird-raised son and the daughter of a demon's line?

events.label: The stars favour the match
events.summary: Sam's star-readers search the heavens and tell him with smiles that a mighty hero will be born of Zal and the daughter of Mehrab, who will bring the world under his sword and be Iran's hope. Sam consents and promises to go to the king.

events.label: Sindokht discovers the secret
events.summary: A go-between carries the good news and Rudabeh's gifts for Zal. Sindokht catches her, finds royal jewels on her and confronts her daughter; Rudabeh weeps and confesses that she and Zal have pledged themselves and that Sam has already answered.

events.label: Mehrab's fury
events.summary: Sindokht tells Mehrab, who draws his sword to kill Rudabeh, fearing the wrath of Sam and the king will burn Kabul. Sindokht holds him back, reminds him that Fereydun too married into Yemen, and makes him swear not to harm their daughter; Rudabeh stands before her father, unashamed of her choice.

events.label: The king's fear
events.summary: Manuchehr hears of the bond between Zal and Mehrab and fears that a child of Zahhak's line could bring turmoil to Iran. He sends Nowzar, his son, to summon Sam from his wars.

events.label: Sam's victory over Kakuy
events.summary: At court Sam tells the king of his war: the fierce warriors of the Gorgsaran and Mazandaran, and their champion Kakuy, whom he pulled from the saddle by his belt and dashed to the ground, after which the enemy fled.

events.label: A command against Kabul
events.summary: Manuchehr commands Sam to go to Hindustan, burn the palace of Mehrab and Kabul, and leave none of the kin of Zahhak alive. Sam promises to obey and sets out for home.

events.label: Zal faces his father
events.summary: Zal rides to meet Sam and reproaches him: abandoned as a baby, raised by a bird, he has kept his father's every word, and now his father comes to destroy his home; let him saw him in two instead. Sam admits his injustice and writes to Manuchehr, recounting his long service – among it the slaying of the dragon of the Kashaf river with his ox-headed mace – and asking the king to grant Zal's wish.

events.label: Sindokht's plan
events.summary: When the news reaches Kabul, Mehrab threatens to kill Sindokht and Rudabeh to appease the king. Sindokht asks instead to go to Sam herself with treasure, makes Mehrab promise to keep Rudabeh safe, and sets out with gold, horses, servants, elephants and a jewelled throne.

events.label: Sindokht before Sam
events.summary: Sindokht comes to Sam as an envoy of Mehrab and lays the treasures before him; he accepts them for Zal. Pleading for the innocent people of Kabul, she obtains his pledge of safety and only then reveals that she is Mehrab's wife and Rudabeh's mother. Sam promises safety to all of Kabul and consents to the marriage.

events.label: Zal at court
events.summary: Zal reaches Manuchehr's court and kisses the ground. The king reads Sam's letter, smiles and, though still uneasy, promises to grant Zal's wish, and keeps him at his side.

events.label: The king's star-readers
events.summary: Manuchehr's mobads and astrologers study the heavens for three days and declare that a hero of long life, strength and glory will be born of Zal and Mehrab's daughter, the refuge of the riders of Iran.

events.label: The riddles
events.summary: The mobads test Zal with riddles: twelve trees of thirty branches, two racing horses, thirty riders one of whom vanishes, a reaper in a meadow, a bird on two cypresses, and a city on a mountain. Zal answers each – the months of the year, day and night, the waning moon, time that reaps all, the halves of the year, and this passing world and the lasting one – and then outshines every rider in feats of arms. The king gives him rich gifts.

events.label: Good news to Kabul
events.summary: Manuchehr writes to Sam that Zal's wish is granted. Zal sends word ahead, and Sam sends a rider to Mehrab; Mehrab praises Sindokht's wisdom, and she tells Rudabeh, who thanks her mother, while Kabul is decked out for the celebration.

events.label: Father and son together
events.summary: Zal returns to Sam, who tells him smiling of Sindokht's visit and her pledge. Seeing his son's joy, Sam orders the march to Kabul and sends word ahead to Mehrab.

entityAssociations.role: father who leads them to Kabul

events.label: The wedding
events.summary: Mehrab rides out with music and elephants to meet Sam and Zal, and Sindokht welcomes Sam with three hundred maids. Sam is amazed at Rudabeh; the marriage is made by rite, and weeks of feasting follow. All then go to Sistan, where Sam gives the rule to Zal and leaves to make war in the Gorgsaran.

events.label: The Simorgh's counsel
events.summary: Rudabeh grows heavy with child and suffers until she faints. Zal remembers the Simorgh's feather and burns part of it; the bird appears, foretells a lion-hearted son, and tells him how a skilled man is to open her side after making her drunk with wine, then sew and heal the wound with herbs, milk and musk and a stroke of her feather.

events.label: The birth of Rostam
events.summary: A skilled mobad opens Rudabeh's side and brings out a child of wondrous size, then sews the wound. When she wakes she says she is delivered – «rastam» – and the boy is named Rostam. A silk figure of the child, armed and on horseback, is sent to Sam, who rejoices; Rostam drinks the milk of ten nurses and at eight is as tall as a cypress.

events.label: Sam meets his grandson
events.summary: Sam comes to see the boy, who rides out on an elephant with mace and shield and greets his grandfather as a servant eager for armour and war. They feast for a month; Mehrab, drunk, boasts that he will revive the ways of Zahhak, and Zal and Sam laugh. At the month's end Sam counsels Zal to justice, says he feels his time is near, and returns to his wars in the West.
